source_text: Τῶν δ’ ἀμφὶ τὸν Μοντανὸν καὶ Ἀλκιβιάδην καὶ Θεόδοτον περὶ τὴν Φρυγίαν ἄρτι τότε πρῶτον τὴν περὶ τοῦ προφητεύειν ὑπόληψιν παρὰ πολλοῖς ἐκφερομένων πΛεῖσται γὰρ οὖν καὶ ἄλλαι παραδοξοποιίαι τοῦ θείου χαρίσματος εἰς ἔτι τότε κατὰ διαφόρους ἐκκλησίας ἐκτελούμεναι πίστιν παρὰ πολλοῖς τοῦ κἀκείνους προφητεύειν παρεῖχον) καὶ δὴ διαφωνίας ὑπαρχούσης περὶ τῶν δεδηλωμένων, αὖθις οἱ κατὰ τὴν Γαλλίαν ἀδελφοὶ τὴν ἰδίαν κρίσιν καὶ περὶ τούτων εὐλαβῆ καὶ ὀρθοδοξοτάτην ὑποτάττουσιν, ἐκθέμενοι καὶ τῶν παρ’ αὐτοῖς τελειωθέντων μαρτύρων διαφόρους ἐπιστολάς, ἃς ἐν δεσμοῖς ἔτι ὑπάρχοντες τοῖς ἐπ’ Ἀσίας καὶ Φρυγίας ἀδελφοῖς διεχάραξαν, οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ Ἐλευθέρῳ τῷ τότε Ῥωμαίων ἐπισκόπῳ, τῆς τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν εἰρήνης ἕνεκα πρεσβεύοντες.
pass_a_gloss: Of those around Montanus and Alcibiades and Theodotus in Phrygia at that time first then the opinion about prophesying being brought forth by many, for many other paradoxical things of the divine gift were being performed even then in various churches, providing faith to many that also those were prophesying, and since there was disagreement about the things declared, again the brothers in Gaul submit their own judgment and about these things, being cautious and most orthodox, having sent also various letters of the martyrs who had been perfected among them, which they had written while still in bonds to the brothers in Asia and Phrygia, but also to Eleutherus who was then bishop of the Romans, acting as ambassadors for the sake of the peace of the churches
pass_b_english: The movement around Montanus, Alcibiades, and Theodotus in Phrygia first brought the question of prophecy to the fore. Many were convinced that these men were genuine prophets because so many other striking works of the divine gift were still being performed in various churches. Since disagreement arose over these matters, the brothers in Gaul once again submitted their own judgment on the question, doing so with great caution and complete orthodoxy. They sent various letters from the martyrs who had been perfected among them, letters those martyrs had written while still in prison to the brothers in Asia and Phrygia, and also to Eleutherus, who was then bishop of Rome, acting as ambassadors for the sake of the peace of the churches.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex syntax of the Greek sentence. Pass A provides a literal rendering of the clauses, and Pass B provides a fluent English version that preserves all nuances, including the causal relationship between the 'paradoxical things' and the 'faith' provided to many, the character of the Gallic brothers (cautious and orthodox), and the specific recipients of the letters (Asia, Phrygia, and Eleutherus).
